title: The naive framing: "just pick the smartest model?"
text: A newcomer might think the smartest model is always the right pick. It's not the smartest, it's the frontier. The cheapest model that still clears your bar. So, which model actually belongs there?

title: Stakes: three models, one task, expensive to try all three
text: Three Claude models can do your task, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, and trying all three on real traffic before you decide is expensive. The natural read, grab

title: The wrong guess: grab an extreme (accuracy or price)
text: Opus for the accuracy or grab Haiku for the price. Either extreme feels like the safe choice. Hold on to one shape, the

title: The anchor: the pareto frontier, abstract
text: Pareto frontier, the curve of models where you can't buy more accuracy without paying more or cut cost without losing it.

title: Broken, with a case: both extremes lose on a real task
text: Test a real task, customer support classification, and both extremes lose. Opus's extra accuracy costs double Sonnet's price for the same job. Haiku saves 3 cents but drops eight points.

title: Mechanism: the sweep — same suite, two numbers per model
text: Finding the frontier takes a sweep. Run every model on the same eval suite and record two numbers per model, accuracy and cost per call.

title: Mechanism: non-dominated — the frontier rule
text: Plot accuracy against cost. A model sits on the frontier only if no other model beats it on one axis without losing on the other.

title: The one flag: illustrative cost/quality numbers
text: The plain numbers for this example, Opus runs $15 in 75 out per million tokens. Sonnet three and 15. Haiku a quarter and a $1.25. Quality 98, 90, 82%. Check current pricing before you decide, these numbers move.

title: The anchor returns: real dots on the frontier
text: Same shape, real dots. Haiku 1 cent, 82%. Sonnet 4 cents, 90% on the frontier. Opus 8 cents, 98. Sonnet saves $4,000 per 100,000 calls.

title: Both directions (A): high threshold, Opus only
text: Need 95% or higher? The frontier only has one point that clears it, Opus. There the extra cost is the price of the accuracy you actually need. 82% is

title: Both directions (B): low threshold, Haiku wins
text: Enough for your task, then Haiku is the frontier point and Sonnet's extra accuracy is money you didn't need to spend.

title: Carry-out
text: The right model isn't the smartest one or the cheapest one. It's whichever one sits on the frontier for your task, and a sweep is the only way to find it. Your

title: Your turn
text: Turn. Here's the prompt, read it with me. Sweep my task across Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku. Plot cost versus accuracy and tell me which model sits on the Pareto frontier for me. Lay 'em in for bare.

title: Outro
text: The Pareto frontier, finding the cheapest model that solves your task. Lay 'em in for bare.
